method: Direct original-image regions and observed front-elevation relationships; no freeform replacement architecture
limitations: Rectangular source regions overlap and are not solid-object masks. Front projection does not establish hidden rear depth, footprint or numerical module interfaces.

principal_regions.title: Western original connected ranges
principal_regions.observed: Two dominant great-window bays, lower curved/returning arcades, smaller upper gallery bays, roof-garden setbacks and attached star-panel projections

principal_regions.title: Eastern original connected ranges
principal_regions.observed: Two great-window bays at the left of the range; longer nested/angled ward fronts and projections to the right; different levels and lengths from the west

principal_regions.title: Western lower arcade and projections
principal_regions.observed: Small pointed glazed bays with solid rose/ivory masonry, stepped garden roofs and projecting star-panel bastion

principal_regions.title: Eastern nested wards and changing fronts
principal_regions.observed: Several connected unequal-length fronts, glazed medium/small bays, recessed terraces and a lower stair return; not a uniform repeated arcade

principal_regions.title: Broad western onion pavilion above the wing
principal_regions.observed: Large wide onion-roof pavilion visually above/behind the western hero-window range; must not be replaced by a small dome at an arbitrary wing end

principal_regions.title: Eastern projecting belvedere and wing attachment
principal_regions.observed: Tall projecting pale/rose body, glazed gallery and plum dome integrated into the eastern composition

principal_regions.title: Eastern spire cluster behind the wards
principal_regions.observed: Unequal close-set tall stems and attached extensions behind the eastern wards; existing positions control

principal_regions.title: Western great-window pair — original positions
principal_regions.observed: The two actual west great bays. Reuse the selected single-bay master twice at these source positions, not a generic new row of small open arches

principal_regions.title: Original ceremonial gate and gable
principal_regions.observed: Principal entry axis and gable; source composition is slightly offset, not forced to perfect symmetry

principal_regions.title: Original complete stair and cascade axis
principal_regions.observed: Central wet spine and two dry flanking flights connect to the original gate/terrace junction; do not rearrange them to suit a generated module

principal_regions.title: Western source assembly with its actual upper pavilion and lower wings
principal_regions.observed: Exact original front-projection context, including associated towers and gardens; not a newly invented isolated wing or a measured footprint

principal_regions.title: Eastern source assembly with its actual spires and nested wards
principal_regions.observed: Exact original front-projection context, including associated towers and gardens; not a newly invented isolated wing or a measured footprint

reuse_bindings.placement: Two actual west bays plus two actual east bays flanking the existing gate; one master per bay
Existing smaller set-back ranges and gallery faces
Triangular rose wall fields over the selected great and smaller bays
Actual roof/terrace contours, with curved and returning profiles
Existing pier faces and bracket positions; no new arbitrary lamp rhythm
Existing roof terraces and source garden pockets; reuse rather than create a new planting composition

rejected_changes: Open colonnades replacing solid stained-glass wing walls
A decorative two-bay building invented independently of the source tier layout
Changed wing lengths, front planes and roof setbacks
Moved or substituted onion pavilions, projecting towers and attached stems
Uniform repeated arch rhythm replacing the hierarchy of great, medium and small windows
Assuming matching marble, glass and carving alone makes the structure match
next_step: Use these exact regions to establish the structural assembly/placement graph. Reuse the original images as canonical references. Do not generate another wing silhouette before the front correspondence and unresolved depth have been recorded.
